 Trump has a plan to limit student loans for nursing and other advanced degrees. A new bill would reverse those cuts.

 Democratic lawmakers are pushing to expand access to higher student-loan borrowing limits .
 On Tuesday, Sens. Kirsten Gillibrand and Jeff Merkley introduced a bill that would expand the number of advanced degrees that qualify for a professional degree designation and thus a higher borrowing cap.
 President Donald Trump's student-loan repayment overhaul placed a $100,000 lifetime borrowing cap on graduate degrees and a $200,000 cap on professional degrees. The administration also planned to limit professional degrees to 11 programs, such as medicine and law, while excluding other programs like nursing, social work, and education.
 The limits were met with criticism by both Democratic and Republican lawmakers who argued that limiting borrowing for nurses would exacerbate the healthcare worker shortage. A lawsuit blocked the administration from implementing the new limits on July 1, and the Democratic lawmakers are now seeking to codify professional status for an expanded list of degrees .
 "Nurses, teachers, and social workers are dedicated public servants, and Congress must do everything it can to help recruit the next generation of these heroes," Merkley said in a statement. "We're already facing a shortage of these critical workers, and new limits on federal student loans for these professions and others threaten to further jeopardize the future of our workforce."
 The bill would maintain professional status for programs that already qualify while restoring professional status to additional programs, including nursing, public health, and physician assistant programs. It would also give the education secretary the flexibility to add more programs that meet the "professional degree" requirements.
 It follows a bipartisan bill earlier this year that called for the inclusion of advanced nursing degrees on the list of professional degrees, noting that tuition for some programs exceeded the borrowing cap. The Department of Education previously said that most advanced nursing programs borrow within the limits.
 After a blue wave in the midterms, Democratic lawmakers said they plan to bolster oversight of the student-loan industry and Trump's repayment changes through hearings, investigations, and legislation. Gillibrand said in a statement that students pursuing fields like social work or nursing "should not have to break the bank to serve their communities."
 "This bill would help our students, our universities, and our communities, and I'm determined to get it passed," she said.
